name: Rowing Blazers
why: New York label from 2017, rugby shirts and striped blazers with a wink, founded by a rower and historian; one store, Elizabeth Street, majority-owned by Burch Creative Capital.
origin: Founded in 2017 in New York, NY, USA by Jack Carlson (with co-founder David Rosenzweig).

marks: NONE: no licensed or proprietary technical fabric named on any of 140 men's PDPs (sherpa fleece is unbranded 100% polyester
Our Values names Cashball, which no men's style in the navigation carries)

craft_evidence.owned: no: Our Values says products are made "in workshops, factories, and mills" in Portugal and the United States, none named or owned; no owned factory found
craft_evidence.makers: no: 0 of 140 men's PDPs name a factory or maker
craft_evidence.mills: no: no mill named on any PDP; "Donegal wool" (1 style) is a yarn type, not a named mill
craft_evidence.madein: 25 of 140 men's PDPs (18%) state a country, all Portugal ("Made in Portugal" or "knit on vintage looms in Portugal"), mostly rugbies; Our Values: "the vast majority of our products in Portugal and the United States"
craft_evidence.heritage: dated: about-us says founded by Jack Carlson in 2017, "a small, young, New York-based team"; no dated heritage before 2017 (the name comes from Carlson's 2014 book Rowing Blazers)
craft_evidence.process: partial: PDPs state fabric weights (220/285/390 gsm), "knit in the traditional 12-gauge style on vintage looms in Portugal" on the heavyweight rugbies, and garment-dyed oxfords; Our Values says end-of-day rugbies and patchwork tweed are made from upcycled fabric scraps
craft_evidence.reasoning: Rowing Blazers names no factory, maker or mill on any of 140 men's product pages. It states a country (Portugal) on 18% of them, and its values page says most product is made in Portugal and the US in unnamed workshops. The "vintage looms in Portugal" line on the rugbies is the one process claim, and with an unnamed factory it is a claim, not evidence. That is a 2: a country and little else.

ownership.owner: Burch Creative Capital (Chris Burch) majority stake since Feb 2024, with co-investors Tom Vellios (Five Below co-founder) and Jason Epstein (Stonecourt Capital); terms undisclosed. The brand's about-us page: "Since 2024, Rowing Blazers has been a part of the Burch family of brands". Jack Carlson stayed on as creative director, then left in March 2025 (Glossy) and joined J.Press (Hypebeast, Sept 2025)

opview: “From the beginning, I've wanted the brand to reflect my eclectic interests and my philosophy about clothing and style” — Jack Carlson, founder, The Rake, "In Conversation with Jack Carlson of Rowing Blazers"
